THE FIRST REVIEW OF 1.24.34 (a lift station's schematic and the drawings it needs: AI_STATION asks()/WHOLE/ALLDRAW and
the part-and-wire reading partsOf/partRole/fromParts/tookText; floatJob in AI_CONTROL and AI_PUMP_STATION; the open
circuit's line in AI_SCHEMATIC; rest()/rec.more/restHeld in AI_ACTIONS and ASSIST_CHAT; view()'s againHint and header;
the bench question make-liftstation-drawings). Reviewed at d72dd5a (the draft) by a reviewer that did not write it.
1.24.33 as released (0dfc9d8) loaded beside it for every comparison.

HOW TO REPLAY
  node tests/fixtures/liftstation_review1_1234/replay.js [id-prefix]     (jsdom, about 10 s; needs git for 0dfc9d8)
  run_d72dd5a.txt is the run this file reports. load.js is a copy of ../liftstation_review1_1230/load.js (read before
  use); lib.js and every case are this review's own. Each case: {id, harm, input, right, run() -> "" when Lantern does
  right}. Harm: high = a right answer spoiled (a right tool, circuit or float taken away), or a wrong thing drawn or
  handed to the model as right; medium = a wrong line handed back but nothing drawn from it, a wrong thing said beside a
  right drawing, a block lost or shown twice, a question in words offered a block; low = wording, titles, tags.

WHAT WAS RUN, AND WHAT WAS NOT
  Run: every case below in jsdom with a scripted model (Chat turns through L.CHAT.turn, the bench's path through
  aiAct.solve and aiBench.grade). The bench guard replays all 301 bench questions and all 312 distinct model replies
  kept in tests/fixtures/bench_run_*.json through build, solve and whole Chat turns on both versions.
  Not run: no real model (every reply here is written by this reviewer); no browser, so no drawing was looked at; the
  look turn of a model that sees (canSee is false in jsdom); the grammars (the draft does not change them).
  tests/liftstation_1234.js (the draft's own) passes: 28 of 28.

COUNTS
  A which tool (routing; the bench guard)                 65 cases, 27 DISAGREE (8 high, 17 medium, 2 low)
  B part-and-wire blocks read as the station              59 cases, 32 DISAGREE (9 high, 16 medium, 7 low)
  C floatJob: "emergency"                                 34 cases, 14 DISAGREE (6 high, 7 medium, 1 low)
  D the open circuit's line to write                      19 cases,  9 DISAGREE (4 high, 1 medium, 4 low)
  E Chat's other blocks (rec.more, restHeld)              23 cases, 11 DISAGREE (1 high, 7 medium, 3 low)
  F the failure's advice, the header, the bench question  21 cases,  3 DISAGREE (0 high, 0 medium, 3 low)
  In all: 221 cases: 125 AGREE, 96 DISAGREE (28 high, 48 medium, 20 low), in 17 root causes below.

WHAT HOLDS (the guard agrees)
  - Adam's question goes to MAKE STATION alone, and the 35B's two blocks make the station: control, piping, levels,
    H2 off, H1 lead (said), H3 alarm, gate valves, both blocks taken in and neither made again (A-01, B-01, E-01, E-09).
  - Every bench question keeps its tool, split and prompt; every ideal solves and grades as on 1.24.33; all 312 saved
    replies build, solve and run through Chat with the same rec.made, calls and notes (A-60..A-64). The bench's path
    (solve) never calls rest(): rec.made / out.made are unchanged.
  - Fire, booster, irrigation, chilled water and compressor stations, programs, decks, SOPs, checklists, budgets, songs
    and essays keep their tools (A-24..A-30, A-48..A-57); a station with a deck or a program is split (A-58, A-59).
  - Many right part-and-wire blocks read right: float parts, LS-tagged sensors with plain job names, "Float - Off"
    switches, level probes, LSL/LSH/LSHH, swing checks and plug valves, force main and gravity inlet, suction valves
    left out and said, vent/air release/drain valves not taken, a redundant off kept, lamps, push buttons, HOA,
    selectors, contactors and non-level sensors not taken, four pumps, a one-pump sump (B-01..B-27).
  - "Emergency High" is the alarm in MAKE CONTROL and MAKE STATION; emergency off/stop are off (C-01..C-15, C-32..C-36).
  - The 35B's open circuit gets "wire G1 V1" and is made once written; plain chains get the right line; two places,
    no line (D-01..D-10).
  - Chat: a circuit and a table in one reply are both shown; a question in parts keeps its own way; a table held
    across a correction is shown after it; the instructions' example and a repeated block are not made; a station's
    drawings' blocks are not made again (E-01..E-12).
  - The failure's advice: shapes only for a drawing, rows only for a sheet, "Ask again." for the rest; the header
    names a pump station / a pump station's piping; the bench question passes its ideal and the 35B's reply and fails
    a circuit, a picture, one pump and prose (F-01..F-10, F-20..F-27).

FINDINGS, MOST HARM FIRST

1. HIGH. The new verbs take plans and overviews that 1.24.33 sent elsewhere (A-13..A-17, A-31, A-65 high; A-21, A-22,
   A-23, A-32 medium).
   WHOLE now matches write/give/produce/prepare/provide/generate/put together/draft anywhere within 60 characters of
   "lift station", and SHOWV counts "plan" and "design". These are the verbs of documents and of words. "Write a plan
   for replacing the pumps at our lift station", "Give me a plan for maintaining a lift station", "Put together a
   training plan for lift station operators", "Give me a plan of action for a lift station overflow", "Write up an
   emergency response plan ..." were MAKE PLAN's on 1.24.33 and now get MAKE STATION alone (a whole tool is the only one
   offered). "Give me an overview of lift station design" got no tool on 1.24.33; now, when the model answers in
   words, Chat says "The AI explained instead of writing a MAKE STATION block" and replaces the overview with a drawn
   station (A-65: 2 calls where 1.24.33 made 1). Same for "Give me tips on lift station design", "Give me a lift
   station design calculation", "Write a plan to clean the lift station wet well", "Write a plan to bypass pump ...".
   Expect: the new verbs count only when their object is a drawing ("write/give/provide ... a schematic / the drawings
   / a diagram / a P&ID / a layout of ... lift station"); "plan" (other than "plan view") and "design" standing after
   the station ("lift station design") are not a request to draw. Draw/sketch/lay out/make/create keep what they had.

2. HIGH. ALLDRAW outranks the document and the question asked in words (A-18 high; A-19, A-20, A-33..A-37, A-47
   medium; A-38 low).
   asks() returns true on pk (PACKAGE or ALLDRAW) before it tests OTHER_DOC, so "Write a report listing the drawings a
   lift station requires" (1.24.33: DOC) is MAKE STATION's; so are "Provide a list of drawings required for a lift
   station permit" and "Write the drawing index for a lift station". The words test covers how/why/what/which/when/
   should/explain/describe/tell me only: "Do I need any other drawings for a lift station?", "Are there any other
   drawings a lift station needs?", "Is a P&ID one of the drawings a lift station needs?", "List the drawings a lift
   station needs", "I need to know which drawings a lift station requires" all get MAKE STATION. And foreign() now
   treats ALLDRAW as the station's: "Draw a lift station, and a motor starter circuit with any other drawings it
   needs" lost its split (1.24.33: STATION + CONTROL) -- the starter is gone.
   Expect: ALLDRAW counts only as the object of a make verb, never above OTHER_DOC (report, list, index), never in a
   question (do/does/is/are/list/need to know ... ?), and not in foreign().

3. HIGH. Floats the model wrote are dropped: start/stop outrank the word float; float tags are not read (B-30, B-31,
   B-32).
   NOT_LV (start, stop, run, ...) is tested on the name before LV_NAME, so a switch named "Stop Float", "Lead Start
   Float", "Lag Start Float" is not a float, nor a level sensor LS2 "Lead Pump Start" / LS3 "Lag Pump Start". And a
   switch tagged FS1..FS4 named "Pumps Off", "Lead Pump On", "Lag Pump On" is not a float because the name lacks
   float/level/water -- though AI_STATION's own parse() takes FS/LS/LSH tags as floats. The station is then drawn with
   off, lead and alarm and NO lag float (the second pump never runs with the first), Lantern "assumed: the off and lead
   on floats" that the model wrote, and B-32 says "not carried: FS1-FS3 (switch)" beside a drawing whose FS1 and FS2
   are Lantern's own added floats.
   Expect: the word float or level in the name, or an FS/LS/LSL/LSH/LSHH tag on a switch or sensor, makes it a float;
   NOT_LV excludes only a name with no float/level word; added floats never take a tag the model's block used.

4. HIGH. "Incoming" anything is the inlet (B-33, B-34, B-35).
   partRole gives "inlet" to any part whose name has inlet/influent/inflow/incoming, whatever its type: a breaker
   "Incoming Power" or "Incoming Service", a transformer "Incoming 480V". The piping is drawn with an inlet labelled
   "Incoming Power" and the parts list has "Inlet: Incoming Power". These names are ordinary in a station's power
   schematic. Expect: the inlet only from a pipe or a part with no electrical type, or with sewer/gravity/influent in
   its name; never from a breaker, transformer, switch, source.

5. HIGH. A float's name that ends in a number becomes a height (B-36, B-37 high; B-38 medium).
   fromParts writes `float F1 "Float 1"` and parse()'s inch-mark rule (a digit then " is inches) reads it as
   `"Float 1 in`. Lines handed back to the model invent heights nobody gave: "name its job, like: float F1 "off" 1 in"
   (and every one of Float 1..4 told "off"); a triplex's "Lag 1" and "Lag 2" come back as "two heights for the lag on
   float (1 in and 2 in): write it once, like: float F3 "lag on" 1 in" (one of the two lag floats removed); a duplex's
   "Lag 2" is drawn with Lantern saying "heights were given for F4 (2 in) only". CLAUDE.md: never invent a number; the
   line is for this question with its own numbers.
   Expect: the label carried as a label (the inch rule never applied inside a label fromParts wrote); Lag 1 / Lag 2 of a
   triplex kept as two lag floats; floats with no job sent back without a height and without one job for all.

6. HIGH. "Emergency" makes start floats and cutoff floats into lights (C-16, C-17, C-18, C-30, C-31, C-37 high;
   C-19..C-24, C-26 medium; C-25 low).
   AI_CONTROL's floatJob now returns alarm for emergency + anything but off/stop/shut: "Emergency Start", "Emergency
   Pump Start", "Emergency Run", "Emergency Lead", "Emergency High Level Pump On", "Emergency Lag On", "Emergency High -
   Start Both Pumps", "Emergency Shutdown". In MAKE CONTROL a right duplex with FS3 "emergency high - start both pumps"
   loses its lag call relay (both pumps never run; FS3 becomes a second input to the alarm light), and one with FS0
   "emergency low level cutoff" loses FS0 from the call relays' stops (it becomes a low level light; the pumps run past
   it). MAKE STATION the same (C-37: FS3 and FS4 both alarms). "emergency low" moved from off to a low level alarm --
   ambiguous, and off is the reading that keeps the pumps from running dry. AI_PUMP_STATION's own floatJob (used when
   AI_CONTROL is dropped) excludes start/on/lead/lag and disagrees with AI_CONTROL's on these labels (C-26).
   Expect: emergency is the alarm only when nothing in the label starts, runs, stops or cuts off a pump (start/starts/
   on/run/lead/lag/both/assist/cutoff/cut off/shutdown/low ... as off), the same rule in both modules.

7. HIGH. The ground line is given where the ground is not the end (D-20, D-21, D-22, D-23 high; D-24 medium).
   "the current reaches the ground G1 and goes no further ... like: wire G1 B1" is given whenever the source has one
   wire and one ground is reached -- including when that one wire IS the wire to the ground ("wire B1 G1" or
   "wire B1- G1", the positive forgotten). Written, "wire G1 B1" lays a second wire beside it; onLoop takes the two
   parallel wires as a loop, so the circuit is MADE with the battery shorted and the lamp unpowered (D-20..D-22). When
   a part lies beyond the ground (B1, M1, G1, S1 -- the switch after the ground), "goes no further" is untrue, and
   written the line cuts the switch out: the motor is drawn running with its switch hanging, as made (D-23; R1 left
   out in D-24). Expect: the ground line only when the source's one wire is not to that ground and nothing lies beyond
   the ground (every part reached from the source without passing the ground); otherwise the general advice. (The
   pre-existing onLoop accepting two wires between the same two parts as a closed circuit is what makes D-20 "made".)

8. HIGH. A part-and-wire piping beside a MAKE CONTROL is taken in and not drawn (B-61, E-30).
   Adam's question answered with a MAKE CONTROL and the 35B's piping block: the summary says the piping's pumps, wet
   well, check and shutoff valves were read, r.reads holds the piping block (so rest() does not make it), but sp.show
   is the given views plus views(q) -- control only for this question -- and "Lantern drew the control circuit". The
   piping the model wrote is neither drawn in the station nor shown on its own: Adam's complaint, again. Expect: the
   view a conv block is read for is drawn (sp.show gets c.view), or all three when the question asks for the set.

9. MEDIUM. "Write" spreads "draw"'s reach to the station's other machines (A-41..A-45 medium; A-46 low).
   "Write a schematic for a lift station's alarm dialer / VFDs / SCADA RTU / level transmitter / emergency lighting /
   alarm light" were MAKE SCHEMATIC's on 1.24.33 and are now MAKE STATION's: the station's three drawings for one
   device's wiring. ("Draw a schematic for a lift station's VFDs" already went to MAKE STATION on 1.24.33 -- a
   pre-existing over-reach the new verbs carry to "write".) Expect: a device of the station named as the schematic's
   subject (dialer, VFD, drive, RTU, PLC panel, transmitter, transducer, lighting, heater, alarm light) is its own
   schematic, as the generator and the fan already are.

10. MEDIUM. Things that are not floats sent back as floats, with a line to make them one (B-39..B-44, B-53).
   A level transducer, an ultrasonic level sensor, a switch for the wet well light, vent fan or hatch, a float bypass
   selector: each read as a float with no job, the whole station sent back with "name its job, like: float S9 "high
   level alarm"" (or LT1 "off"). A sump's one float in series with its one pump (it starts and stops it) comes back
   as "float FS1 "off"". Rule 7: the line makes the model's light switch a float. Expect: water/wet well alone is not
   a float's name on a switch (light, fan, hatch, heater, bypass, override join NOT_LV); a transducer/transmitter/
   ultrasonic/radar/bubbler is not carried (said); a lone float with a lone pump is its on/off float, said.

11. MEDIUM. Alarm and status inputs read as level floats (B-45, B-46, B-48 medium; B-47, B-49 low).
   A sensor is a float when its name has any of high/low/on/off/lead/lag/alarm/emergency: "Pump Fail Alarm" and
   "Overtemp Alarm" are drawn as a second high level alarm float (\btemp misses "Overtemp"); "Hatch Alarm" too;
   "Low Battery", "Lead Pump Fail", "Pump 1 On", "Pump 2 On" are said among "the floats" taken and silently merged into
   the model's own floats. Expect: a sensor with no level word is a float only when its whole name is a float's job;
   fail/failure/battery/hatch/overtemp join NOT_LV.

12. MEDIUM. Pumps miscounted or missed (B-51, B-52, B-58).
   An unnamed motor beside "Pump 1" and "Pump 2" (a fan, a mixer) makes a triplex, and the control is then not drawn.
   Unquoted names ("part M1 motor pump 1", a small model's habit) are not pumps: "not carried: M1 (motor pump 1)" and
   "2 pumps: the block did not say" -- both untrue. An electrical block of 2 pumps and a piping block of 3: drawn with
   3, nothing said (MAKE CONTROL beside MAKE PIPING says "check which is meant"). Expect: an unnamed motor is a pump
   only when no motor is named pump; a type ending in a pump's number is a pump; two counts said.

13. MEDIUM. The wet well drawn as "Dry Well" (B-50). The first tank or well part whose name has "well" is the wet
   well; a dry well listed first wins. Expect: wet preferred, dry never the wet well.

14. MEDIUM. Chat draws the station twice (E-20, E-21, E-22).
   A MAKE STATION block followed by a part-and-wire schematic of the same station, or by a MAKE CONTROL or MAKE PIPING,
   gets a second whole station in rec.more, made from that block alone (its own floats, piping and levels; with
   E-27 below, a 3-pump and a 2-pump station side by side). The station action does not read the blocks beside it,
   and rest() builds each through the wrapper as a station question. Expect: after a MAKE STATION, the drawings'
   blocks are read with it (or named as not drawn), not made into another station.

15. MEDIUM. Chat: blocks lost, or prose shown as a block (E-23, E-24, E-25, E-27 medium; E-26, E-29 low).
   - E-24: the first block sent back and the correction answered in prose: the table held from the first reply is
     never shown -- the very failure of Adam's chat (a block neither made nor mentioned).
   - E-23: two circuits with the same title, the first sent back: the held second (a right circuit) is dropped,
     because the filter compares kind and title only with the corrected block.
   - E-25, E-26: "**Make sure:** the battery is 9 V ..." and "Make note: ..." after a block are found as MAKE blocks
     and shown as "Lantern could not make it: ** the battery is 9 V ... Nothing was made: Lantern cannot make a sure;
     it can make: schematic, drawing, ...". rest() should build only blocks whose kind is an action's.
   - E-27: the instructions' example copied with one capital changed ("Lift Station") is made as a second station.
   - E-29: a held table rewritten under another title in the corrected reply is shown twice.

16. LOW (B-57 MEDIUM). What is said (B-56, B-57, B-59, B-60, E-28).
   Floats tagged FA-FD are said taken as FA-FD and drawn FS1-FS4 (fromParts drops a tag with no digit); F1 "Pumps Off"
   said taken and merged into F0 "Low Water Cutoff" (B-57, medium: the model's redundant low-water cutoff below its off
   float is merged away, not drawn, and the summary says both were taken); the 35B's station has no lag float and nothing says
   the second pump never runs with the first (its note says pump 2 starts on a further rise); the 35B's "Discharge
   Header" (P3) is said not carried beside a piping that draws one; Chat's note says "Lantern checked the MAKE
   STATION block" when the AI wrote MAKE SCHEMATIC.

17. LOW. Small things (B-54, B-55, D-25..D-28, F-11, F-12, F-28).
   An influent sluice gate makes the discharge shutoff valves gate valves; the title "Lift Station Pumps and Valves"
   becomes "Lift Station Pumps and"; a ground line is given where a second dead end exists on a side branch (the
   draft's own "two or more places: the model's to say" not applied when one of them is a ground -- the 35B's R2 has
   such dead ends too, S5 and S7, and there the line is right); "fewer rows help" under an empty table and "fewer,
   bigger shapes help" under an empty drawing; the bench passes a "typical lift station" with no high level alarm
   (the check is make-liftstation's, which does not ask for one).

QUESTIONS FOR ADAM (judgement, not code)
  - Finding 6: a float labelled "emergency low" -- read as a redundant off (stops the pumps) or as a low level alarm
    light? 1.24.33 read off; the draft reads the light.
  - Finding 1: should "give me ... a lift station" offer MAKE STATION at all, or only when a drawing word is the object?
